lines: Over forty degrees, and no electricity. Open a window? You just let the heat in. So how do you cool this room?
Problem one: the sun bakes the walls. Fix: mud brick, laid very thick. It soaks up the heat of the day, so the room stays cooler.
Problem two: the air inside just sits there. Fix: a tower. Up above the roofs, the wind blows stronger and cooler, with less dust.
Problem three: the wind keeps changing direction. Fix: walls inside the tower split it into shafts. One side always catches the wind and pushes it down.
Problem four: hot air needs a way out. Fix: the far side of the tower. Wind rushing past creates suction, pulling stale air up and out.
Problem five: desert wind is hot. Fix: water. In a cellar, water from an underground canal evaporates, and the air comes up cooler.
Problem six: no wind. Fix: the sun. It heats the tower, the air inside rises, and that draws cool air up from the cellar.
It can be eight to twelve degrees cooler inside. No motor, no fuel, no noise. One of these towers, in Yazd, Iran, stands thirty three meters tall.
